historical_reviews.deepseek: Unlike the preceding range cases, its exact sensor query can address the named record. It still lacks the approved meaning/location of IBC, expected thresholds, complete inventory and both Web views.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly gates execution on IBC mapping and protects the correlated power path. This review refuses to expand the acronym and requires component-to-rail provenance before interpreting temperature.
historical_reviews.duplicate_search: No duplicate code exists; adjacent RTM and rear-board sensors are distinct thermal locations.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-36 makes component identity, topology and expected sensor semantics readiness inputs; ED-38 forbids PMBus/power/log changes and preserves engineer verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Validate the single TEMP_UBB_IBC channel for the owner-defined IBC component, confirming its physical and power-path identity, readable temperature and enabled thresholds across exact IPMI evidence, Dashboard and Server Health.
original_method: The power/board owner defines IBC and its UBB location/rail relationship, maps the named sensor to both Web views and supplies temperature limits and threshold enablement; automation then collects complete passive evidence for operator comparison.
manual_activity: The power/board owner defines IBC, identifies its component, location and associated rail, supplies temperature limits and threshold masks and confirms the exact entry in both BMC-Web views.
required_inputs: Authoritative IBC expansion/function for this platform and component PN/revision
IBC physical UBB location and associated input/output power path or rail
Exact SDR record/entity and Dashboard/Server Health mapping
Temperature measurement point, units, scaling, tolerance, freshness and unavailable semantics
Enabled threshold mask and expected lower/upper noncritical, critical and nonrecoverable values
Expected operating range with ambient/load/power context
BMC/SDR/IBC firmware versions, secret-safe OOB access and complete evidence collector
IBC/rail thermal aborts and independent power/BMC recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not assume what IBC stands for or substitute another board/rail sensor
Verify the exact named record belongs to the approved IBC component and power path
Retain the complete SDR inventory for entity/duplicate checks; the first 100 lines are insufficient
Interpret only enabled thresholds and distinguish temperature from voltage/current/power telemetry
Do not issue PMBus, power, threshold, firmware, reset or log-clear commands
Stop on missing/stale/invalid reading, abnormal IBC or rail temperature, threshold mismatch or management instability
Protect credentials and do not automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact source identity and owner-defined IBC component/rail mapping
Capture complete read-only SDR inventory and exact TEMP_UBB_IBC output
Parse temperature, units, state, freshness and enabled thresholds
Prepare matching Dashboard and Server Health entries for operator confirmation
Correlate passive rail, PSU, fan, SEL and BMC health
Perform no PMBus/power/threshold/BMC change or final verdict
engineer_actions: Define IBC and approve its component/location/rail identity
Provide operating range and enabled threshold values
Confirm both Web mappings and interpretation of unavailable fields
Review evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The exact `sensor get 'TEMP_UBB_IBC'` is a relevant passive query, but password-in-argv is unsafe, the fallback is truncated and neither IBC provenance nor Web thresholds are proven.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After owner mapping, use approved secret-safe OOB access to retain the full SDR inventory and exact sensor output with threshold flags, then compare its identity, value and enabled thresholds with both Web entries and the IBC specification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact TEMP_UBB_IBC name, two Web paths, reading/threshold criterion and 1/1-minute estimates are preserved; the acronym, rail and values are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES IBC COMPONENT/RAIL AND THRESHOLD PACKAGE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the single named sensor to its physical component and power path, capture exact plus full-inventory evidence, normalize only enabled thresholds and reconcile the same record in both Web views.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing component/rail provenance and completes Web/threshold evidence without treating the truncated fallback as authoritative.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An exact sensor name can still be stale, duplicated or mapped to the wrong component; a readable value does not prove the threshold configuration or power-path identity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Collection is passive, but false attribution can hide heating in a safety-critical power component.

project_override_considerations: If the project officially defines IBC through a vendor document, cite that revision and sensor placement. Designs with redundant or multiple IBCs require explicit coverage or a source correction rather than assuming the singular row covers all devices.
expected_evidence: Approved IBC definition, component PN/revision, UBB location and rail relationship
Exact SDR record/entity and both Web mappings
Measurement point, value, units, state, freshness and enabled-threshold table
Complete redacted SDR plus exact sensor output with status/timestamps

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row consistently targets one named IBC temperature sensor and its Web threshold. The acronym and expected values are undefined but no alternate target is asserted.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A passive exact-sensor validation path is identifiable. IBC component identity, rail topology and expected thresholds are normal project readiness inputs under ED-36.

review_improvement: Preserves the valid exact read while adding component-to-rail provenance, complete inventory and threshold enablement, and prevents the IBC acronym or power semantics from being guessed.
independent_technical_reasoning: A unique string match is not sufficient engineering identity for a power-related temperature channel. Without a component and rail map, a plausible reading cannot be correlated with the correct blast radius or operating limits. The named record can be collected safely, but interpretation and Web acceptance must remain gated on the owner-approved IBC definition and threshold table.
